questions.stem: Kanchipuram Silk Saree, famous for its heavy pure-silk fabric and contrasting borders woven with zari, holds a GI tag from which state?

options.option_text: Karnataka, known for Mysore silk weaving traditions
Tamil Nadu, where Kanchipuram has woven silk for centuries
Andhra Pradesh, home to several major silk weaving clusters
Telangana, known for its Pochampally silk weaving heritage

questions.explanation: Kanchipuram (also spelled Kancheepuram) is a town in Tamil Nadu, and its distinctive silk sarees received a GI tag recognising Tamil Nadu as the origin. Karnataka is a tempting distractor because it has its own GI-tagged Mysore Silk, but the two are different products from different states.

questions.stem: The Geographical Indications Registry — India's sole authority that examines and grants GI tags — is located in which city?

options.option_text: New Delhi, seat of the Ministry of Commerce and DPIIT
Mumbai, home to the Intellectual Property India headquarters
Chennai, where the GI Registry functions under the CGPDTM
Kolkata, the historic seat of the first Indian Patent Office

questions.explanation: The GI Registry operates in Chennai under the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM). New Delhi is a common wrong answer because DPIIT (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade), which oversees IP policy, is based there — but the operational registry itself is in Chennai.

questions.stem: Pochampally Ikat, a handloom textile famed for its geometric resist-dyed patterns where threads are tie-dyed before weaving, received a GI tag from which state?

options.option_text: Odisha, where the similar Sambalpuri Ikat tradition originates
Andhra Pradesh, the parent state of Pochampally before 2014
Telangana, where Pochampally village is currently situated
West Bengal, known for its Jamdani and Tant handloom weaves

questions.explanation: Pochampally village lies in Yadadri Bhongir district of Telangana, making Telangana the GI tag holder. Andhra Pradesh is the single most tempting wrong answer because Pochampally was part of undivided Andhra Pradesh before the 2014 bifurcation — but post-bifurcation, the village and its GI belong to Telangana. Odisha has its own distinct Sambalpuri Ikat tradition, not Pochampally Ikat.

questions.stem: Which of the following was the FIRST temple prasadam (consecrated religious offering) in India to receive a Geographical Indication tag?

options.option_text: Nathdwara Prasad from the Pushti Marg temple in Rajasthan
Tirupati Laddu from the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, AP
Vrindavan Peda, a milk-based sweet from UP's temple town
Shirdi Prasad from the famous Sai Baba temple in Maharashtra

questions.explanation: Tirupati Laddu (also called Srivari Laddu) received its GI tag in 2009, making it the first temple prasadam in India to be so protected. Palani Panchamirtham (Tamil Nadu) is another GI-tagged temple prasad but received it only in 2021, nearly 12 years later. The other options have no GI tag recognition.

questions.stem: Which GI-tagged product is uniquely registered as a JOINT Geographical Indication shared between two different Indian states?

options.option_text: Darjeeling Tea, registered exclusively under West Bengal's GI
Kolhapuri Chappal, jointly registered by Maharashtra and Karnataka
Banaras Brocades, registered exclusively under Uttar Pradesh
Kanchipuram Silk, registered exclusively under Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: Kolhapuri Chappal is a rare example of a jointly held GI tag, shared between Maharashtra and Karnataka, because artisans producing the traditional hand-crafted leather sandal are concentrated in border districts of both states. Darjeeling Tea, Banaras Brocades, and Kanchipuram Silk each belong exclusively to a single state.

questions.stem: Unlike a trademark, a Geographical Indication registered under India's GI Act, 1999 CANNOT legally be:

options.option_text: Renewed upon expiry by paying the prescribed renewal fees
Assigned, licensed, or transmitted to any person or entity
Used collectively by all eligible producers from the region
Opposed by aggrieved parties before the GI Appellate Board

questions.explanation: Under Section 24 of the GI Act, 1999, a registered GI is not an assignable or transmissible right — it cannot be licensed, sold, or franchised to parties outside the producing region, because it belongs to the collective community of producers, not to any individual. This is the fundamental legal distinction from a trademark, which can be assigned and licensed. Renewal, collective use, and Appellate Board challenges are all permitted under the Act.

questions.stem: Muga Silk, a rare golden-coloured natural silk unique in the world, holds a GI tag from which state, and is produced exclusively by which silkworm species?

options.option_text: West Bengal; Bombyx mori silkworm reared on mulberry leaves
Assam; Antheraea assamensis, which feeds on Som and Soalu leaves
Meghalaya; Antheraea mylitta, the wild Tasar silkworm species
Manipur; Philosamia ricini, the castor-feeding Eri silkworm

questions.explanation: Muga Silk is exclusive to Assam and is produced by Antheraea assamensis, a semi-domesticated silkworm that feeds on Som (Machilus bombycina) and Soalu (Litsaea polyantha) leaves, giving the silk its characteristic golden lustre. It is the only naturally golden silk in the world and holds a GI tag for Assam. Option C is wrong because Antheraea mylitta produces Tasar (not Muga) silk, predominantly in Jharkhand and Odisha. Option D confuses Muga with Eri silk from Manipur/Assam, which uses Philosamia ricini and feeds on castor leaves.
